title: Lesson 35: RAG at Scale: Ingestion Pipelines, Refresh, Versioning, and Deletion
description: The write side of RAG: an ingestion pipeline that parses and chunks on the way in, a refresh strategy that re-embeds only what changed, versioning for documents and embedding models, and deletion that actually removes content.

questions.question: Per the lesson "RAG at Scale: Ingestion Pipelines, Refresh, Versioning, and Deletion", what framing makes the write side of RAG click?
options: Treat your embeddings as a materialized view over your source data: derived, expensive to compute, written once, queried often, and assumed correct downstream
Treat the index as a nightly backup of the source system
Treat documents as immutable once they have been embedded
Treat retrieval as a pure cache with no freshness requirement
questions.explanation: The lesson borrows the materialized-view framing from data warehousing and says that once you see embeddings that way, the questions about source of truth, freshness, backfill, and deletes become obvious.

questions.question: The lesson names a failure mode where the vectors stay frozen while the world keeps moving. What is it called?
options: The index is a photograph: vectors are frozen from the moment of embedding, so the assistant answers confidently from a policy that has since changed
questions.explanation: The lesson uses the photograph framing to explain that staleness degrades retrieval quality silently and confidently, because a stale chunk looks identical to a current one.

questions.question: What does the lesson say about deletion in a RAG system?
options: Deleting content in the source system automatically removes the vectors
Deletion is unnecessary as long as refresh runs often enough
A vector database is separate from the source system, so a deletion does not propagate on its own and must be treated as a first-class operation in the pipeline
Deletion only matters for text documents, never for structured records
questions.explanation: The lesson defines deletion as removing content from retrieval when the source removes it or access is revoked, and says the separation between vector store and source means the pipeline must handle it explicitly.
